title: PUSECGIS MVP Specification
author: BJC Public Safety / Hermes Brainstorming
subject: Common Operating Picture Platform MVP — Barnes-Jewish Hospital Public Safety

elements.text:
Status: Draft 0.1 — Proposal | Date: 2026-09-02
Scope: Barnes-Jewish Hospital Public Safety — Common Operating Picture
Goal: A shared visual map capturing incidents, problem areas, and shift-to-shift information across BJC's campus — broadcast to all satellite offices and ED desks.

What it does: A shared operating map for BJC Public Safety that captures incidents (manual entry from officers/dispatch), visualizes them geographically on campus floor plans, and broadcasts live status to all satellite offices and ED desks.

Why it matters: Currently, shift-to-shift information is lost over radio. Officers walk a floor, note problem areas, agitated patients, duress events — then that knowledge evaporates when shift changes. This tool preserves that information visually.

Who it's for: BJC Public Safety officers, floor rounding staff, Dispatch, and Public Safety leads.

Where it runs: BJC internal network only. No internet dependency.

shifts: id, shift_date, shift_code (DAY/EVE/NIGHT), start_time, end_time, created_at

incidents: id, shift_id, incident_type, location_ref (text), description, status (open/resolved/monitoring), logged_by, created_at, updated_at

shift_handoff: id, shift_id, location_ref (nullable), note, logged_by, created_at

users: id, username, display_name, role (officer/dispatch/lead/admin), active

Auth: POST /api/auth/login, GET /api/auth/me

Incidents (auth required): GET /api/incidents?status=&type=&date=, POST /api/incidents, PUT /api/incidents/:id, DELETE /api/incidents/:id

Broadcast (no auth): GET /api/broadcast/incidents?hours=2, GET /api/broadcast/config

Handoff: GET /api/handoff/notes?shift=&date=, POST /api/handoff/notes

Locations/Users: GET /api/locations?q=, GET /api/users
Officer UI: Map view with incident plotting, quick log form (Type dropdown, Location text/search, Description text), Open/Resolved toggle, Shift handoff note area, Incident list with filters.

Broadcast UI (Kiosk): Fullscreen map with color-coded markers, auto-refresh every 30 seconds, incident sidebar (scrollable, newest at top), shift indicator, filter bar, kiosk-safe (fullscreen, prevents exit, auto-reloads).

rows: Internal only, no SSO for MVP

elements.text:
Phase 1: MVP Core (Weeks 1-3)
• PostgreSQL + PostGIS setup
• FastAPI backend (Incidents, Shifts, Users, Handoff, Auth)
• Officer UI (map, incident entry, filter, handoff)
• Broadcast UI (fullscreen map, sidebar, 30s auto-refresh)
• Kiosk mode script (auto-fullscreen, auto-restart)
• Deploy to BJC internal network
• Smoke test with 2-3 officers

Phase 2: Enhancements (Weeks 4-6)
• Duress alarm CSV import & parser
• Hotspot heatmap overlay
• Floor plan overlay (PDF base map)
• Trend charts / reports (weekly/monthly)
• Exportable reports (PDF/CSV)

Phase 3: Integration (Weeks 7-10)
• Duress alarm system API integration
• Radio/CAD integration (if available)
• Mobile-responsive officer UI
• RBAC (officer vs. lead vs. admin)
• Audit logging & security hardening

• Officers can log incidents (type, location, notes)
• Incidents appear on map in correct colors
• Broadcast screens show all active incidents with 30s auto-refresh
• Broadcast screens display at 1920x1080 without map scrolling
• Shift handoff notes are captured and visible per shift
• 6 display targets can view broadcast simultaneously
• All runs on BJC internal network (no internet dependency)
• CSV duress alarm import works (Phase 2)

1. Floor plan format — PDF exists, are CAD files available?
2. MTF CSV sample — can we get one export?
3. User roster — how many active officers/dispatch?
4. Server specs — VM or bare metal? RAM, storage?
5. Duress alarm system vendor — Cognosos, kontakt.io, etc.? API docs?
6. Severity levels — need 1-5 rating or type is enough?
7. Incident retention — how long should resolved incidents stay visible?
8. Offline mode — should broadcast cache if network drops?
9. Notifications — audible/visual alerts for new incidents?
10. Escalation workflow — auto-escalate persistent incidents?
